22:["$","h2",null,{"children":"Common Health Issues"}]
23:["$","h3",null,{"children":"Tuberculosis (TB)"}]
24:["$","p",null,{"children":"TB is taken seriously in Australia. If your chest X-ray shows abnormalities, you may need further testing. Previous TB history does not automatically disqualify you, but you may need additional documentation and treatment proof."}]
25:["$","h3",null,{"children":"Chronic Conditions"}]
26:["$","p",null,{"children":"Conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or asthma are common and usually manageable. The key is demonstrating that you have the condition under control and will not require excessive healthcare resources."}]
27:["$","h3",null,{"children":"Mental Health"}]
28:["$","p",null,{"children":"Mental health conditions are assessed case by case. Having a mental health condition does not automatically prevent approval. The assessment focuses on whether the condition poses a risk to the community or requires significant resources."}]
29:["$","h3",null,{"children":"Significant Costs"}]
2a:["$","p",null,{"children":"The main concern for chronic conditions is \"significant cost\" to the Australian healthcare system. There are thresholds for what constitutes significant cost. If your condition is likely to cost less than this threshold, it usually will not be a problem."}]
